newsitem.title: UK: LME copper prances higher, nickel gives up gains.
newsitem.headline: LME copper prances higher, nickel gives up gains.

text.p: Copper prices posted a strong finish just above $2,530 resistance on Wednesday after surging to fresh one-year highs during an active afternoon session.
Speculative fund and bank buying, combined with shortcovering, whisked three months prices to a high of $2,539 per tonne in the first ring, traders said.
Copper finished the kerb just lower at $2,531 -- a gain of $24 from Tuesday.
"The big level for copper is $2,530, which is the previous high from May 22. It's certainly not a bad close," said analyst Helen Williamson from brokers Brandeis.

The market was generally neutral to news that the Kennecott Utah Copper Corp's smelter was back on stream and is due to reach full capacity later in the year. The 310,000 short tons per year smelter was shut for 42 days for maintenance.

"If they had announced it was be at full capacity next week that would have sent the market lower. But as it has never actually been working at full capacity the news is more or less neutral," Williamson said.
News that unionised workers at Noranda's copper mine and smelter at Murdochville in Canada had approved a three-year labour deal also had little obvious effect on prices.
The market similarly had already factored in late Tuesday's news that supervisors at Chiles' Chuquicamata mine had voted not to strike.
Cash to threes backwardation was slightly wider at $73/$78.
Nickel tried to recover early in the day but failed to hold onto its gains and slipped back below $7,300. It ended at $7,280 versus $7,301 on Tuesday.
It was getting little support from stalled labour talks at Inco's big Sudbury operation in Canada ahead of a May 31 contract expiry.
Aluminium was quiet but firmer with copper at $1,645, up $9. Further consolidation looked likely for aluminium with support around $1,625, anlaysts said.
Zinc was quiet and unchanged at $1,360, after making a foray towards the recent 4-1/2 year high of $1,670.
Lead perked up with copper and was $7 firmer at $641.
But tin lost its footing and slid to the lowest in some three weeks. Prices finished near the day's lows at $5,665, off $65.
